newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan oil workers strike still only a threat.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan oil workers strike still only a threat.

text.p: A possible strike by Venezuelan oil workers in Zulia state over the loss of workers' benefits due to out-sourcing is still only a threat, oil workers union Fedepetrol Secretary General Carlos Ortega told Reuters.
"Next week will be crucial. If we don't find PdVSA responsive, there'll be a union action such as an industry stoppage," he said during a telephone interview.
"But that's not the idea," he added.
Fedepetrol is due to meet next Tuesday with state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) to discuss the threat to workers' benefits of out-sourcing oil operations to the private sector.
"They want to reduce the number of people directly employed in the national oil industry and put them in the hands of the multinationals," he said.

Ortega added that Fedepetrol and other oil union representatives would be meeting this Wednesday to discuss their position and firm a common front against PdVSA and its affiliates Lagoven, Maraven and Pequiven.
